terms.meaning: A stored set of example survey questions with tags.
A number that tells the system which documents to prefer. Higher is preferred.
Following legal and ethical rules about data, such as privacy laws.
A small part of a document that the system stores and searches separately.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Server address and imports
sections.what: Brings in the tool for sending web requests and sets the server address to the local machine on port 8000.
sections.why: Likely reason: the example talks to a server running on this computer.
sections.watch_out: The server must be running before the script starts.

sections.name: load_custom_question_bank (part 1)
sections.title: Question bank text
sections.what: Holds a custom question bank written as plain text with sections, numbered questions and tags for type, scale, topic, category, audience and use case.
sections.why: Likely reason: this text is the content the system will split up and search.
sections.watch_out: The format must match what the ingestion service expects. Mismatched text may load but be used poorly, and that is not visible here.

sections.name: load_custom_question_bank (part 2)
sections.title: Send question bank to the corpus
sections.what: Sends the text with its title, description, type, high priority, use cases, audiences, categories, topics and policy flags to the corpus address.
sections.why: The comment says the high priority makes the system prefer these questions.
sections.watch_out: The priority of 0.95 is higher than the sample loader's values, so this bank wins over those.

sections.name: load_custom_question_bank (part 3)
sections.title: Report the load result
sections.what: On success, prints the new ID, title, type and use cases. Otherwise prints the status code and error text.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms to the user that the load worked.
sections.watch_out: Running the script again loads the bank again, since no duplicate check appears.

sections.name: list_corpus_documents
sections.title: List what is in the corpus
sections.what: Gets all stored documents and prints each one's title, ID, type, audiences and use cases.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the load and shows what the author step can draw on.
sections.watch_out: A failed request prints only the status code, not the error text.

sections.name: load_policy_document (part 1)
sections.title: Policy and compliance text
sections.what: Holds the policy text covering personal data, child privacy, data rights, question design rules and accessibility standards.
sections.why: Likely reason: stored as text so the system can check questions against it.
sections.watch_out: This is a summary, not a complete legal reference. Treat it as a starting point for a compliance review.

sections.name: load_policy_document (part 2)
sections.title: Send policy to the corpus
sections.what: Sends the policy text with top priority and enforcement tags, then prints the new ID or the status code on failure.
sections.why: The comment says the policy has the highest priority and is always enforced.
sections.watch_out: The enforced tag is only a label. Whether any code really enforces it is not visible in this file.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Run all three steps
sections.what: When the file runs directly, loads the question bank, loads the policy, then lists all stored documents.
sections.why: Likely reason: one run sets up the whole example.
sections.watch_out: Running the file again adds the question bank and the policy a second time.

summary: A runnable script that loads a sample question bank and a compliance policy into the document library, then lists what is stored.
purpose: Shows a user how to add their own documents to the corpus.
why: Likely reason: the survey writer uses the stored documents, so the example shows how to add them.
how: Holds two text blocks, sends each with its metadata to the corpus address, and prints the results. Then lists all stored documents.
inputs: Two text blocks written in the script, and a server running at the local address.
outputs: Printed status messages and the list of stored documents.
risks: Running it twice adds duplicate documents. The high priority values change which documents are preferred. The policy text is a summary, not a complete legal reference.
debug: If loading fails, the printout shows the status code and error text. Check that the server is running and that the document type is valid. If the list is empty, confirm the load succeeded.
